text:
cheng: Heads up — NIC firmware rollout to 2.2.0 in us-west1 is toggling secure-boot on a subset of BMCs. OOB sessions dropping, several nodes stuck in GPU provisioning.

alex: How many hosts affected?

cheng: ~48 hosts across two racks, mostly GPU pools p3/p4. Autoscaler queues are spiking, provisioning threads piling up.

infra-bot: Deploy started: nic-fw/2.2.0 -> us-west1-canary (12 hosts). Watching health checks.

maria: If secure-boot flips, kernel procurement fails on the host side and PXE falls back. We should stop the rollout and trigger BMC re-provisioning.

sam_ops: Seeing PM queue latency + failed attach logs: "attach_timeout: 120s" and NVMe attach errors during boot. GPUs stay in provisioning state.

cheng: Paste of bmcctl output for an affected node:
```
# bmcctl get 172.31.64.12
BMC: host-rc-42
secure_boot: true -> was false
oob_state: disconnected
last_fw: nic-fw-2.2.0
logs: tpm: confirm failed, pxe: no-agent
```

alex: Runbook? Can we force BMC secure-boot reset via oobctl?

natalie: Runbook flow: 1) stop firmware rollout 2) set bmc secure-boot policy to inherit 3) re-provision OOB agent 4) drain/recycle nodes. I can lead canary rollback.

maria: Also recommend switching provisioning router to the fallback VLAN so PXE can use legacy TFTP while BMCs are corrected. Minimal config change.

sam_ops: Cost note — fallback to legacy provisioning will increase provisioning time ~3x and keep GPUs locked longer, which will push up committed capacity and short-term billing by ~$6k/day if we keep reserves on. Suggest we prioritize rollback to avoid cost.

alex: Stopping rollout now. infra-bot, abort remaining canaries.

infra-bot: Action: aborting nic-fw/2.2.0 rollout in us-west1. 34 hosts rolled back to 2.1.0.

cheng: Kicking off BMC re-provision on the 48 affected hosts (oobctl re-provision --batch file://hosts-48.txt). Will update when OOB sessions return.

natalie: Can we divert new user traffic away from impacted GPU pools? Set routing rule to prefer eu1/us-central for autoscaler while we fix.

sam_ops: Done — routing rule applied. Autoscaler will prefer fallback pools, reduced risk of failing customer jobs.

infra-bot: Update: 12/48 BMCs re-provisioned, OOB sessions re-established, secure-boot policy now consistent. Provisioning queue length halved.

cheng: Progressing. If we hit a regression after full re-provision, we'll escalate and trigger emergency BIOS rollback on affected hosts.

maria: Postmortem TODOs: add pre-check for BMC secure-boot flag in firmware rollouts, gate NVMe attach regression tests, and add a metric for OOB session drop rate as an early signal.

alex: Agreed. Thanks everyone — keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
